Ofeherto Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ófehértó, Hungary

Not demolished. Ófehértó's Jewish community, never independent (first under Nagykálló, then from 1885 under Kemecse's jurisdiction), maintained a synagogue from the early 19th century and grew from 38 members in 1840 to 143 by 1920. About 15 young Jews were conscripted for forced labor around 1941; on the night of April 14, 1944, Hungarian authorities marched the entire local Jewish population on foot to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto before deportation to Auschwitz. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1857, its newest to 1944; a descendant of Ófehértó's Jews funded fencing in 1988.
